name: tributary_scan_topic

returnsTable.name: topic
returnsTable.description: Topic the message was read from.

returnsTable.name: partition
returnsTable.description: Kafka partition id the message lives in.

returnsTable.name: key
returnsTable.description: Raw message key, `NULL` when the message has none. `JSON` when `schema.registry.url` is set and the `<topic>-key` subject has a JSON schema.

returnsTable.name: message
returnsTable.description: Raw message payload. Use `decode(message)` for UTF-8 text such as JSON (not `message::VARCHAR`, which escapes quotes in DuckDB 2.0). When `schema.registry.url` is set and the `<topic>-value` subject has a JSON schema, this column is named `value` and has type `JSON`.

parameters.name: topic_name
parameters.description: Kafka topic to read. Write it as `kafka://<name>/<topic>` to use the `tributary_cluster` secret scoped to `kafka://<name>`.

parameters.name: bootstrap.servers
parameters.description: Comma-separated `host:port` list of brokers to bootstrap from. Required unless it comes from a `tributary_cluster` secret.

parameters.name: group.id
parameters.description: Consumer group id passed to librdkafka. The scan reads explicit partition ranges and never commits offsets, so it doesn't move a group's position.

parameters.name: security.protocol
parameters.description: `PLAINTEXT`, `SSL`, `SASL_PLAINTEXT`, or `SASL_SSL`. See [Kafka security](https://kafka.apache.org/documentation/#security_ssl).

parameters.name: sasl.mechanism
parameters.description: SASL mechanism — `PLAIN`, `SCRAM-SHA-256`, `SCRAM-SHA-512`, etc. See [Kafka SASL](https://kafka.apache.org/documentation/#security_sasl).

parameters.name: sasl.username
parameters.description: SASL username (PLAIN / SCRAM).

parameters.name: sasl.password
parameters.description: SASL password (PLAIN / SCRAM). Keep it in a `tributary_cluster` secret, or pass it with `getvariable()` from a variable set with `getenv()`, rather than inlining it.

parameters.name: schema.registry.url
parameters.description: Schema Registry URL. When set, the latest JSON schemas of the `<topic>-key` and `<topic>-value` subjects are used to return `key` and `value` as `JSON`. Avro and Protobuf subjects are an error.

Any other librdkafka *global* (client) property from its [CONFIGURATION reference](https://github.com/confluentinc/librdkafka/blob/master/CONFIGURATION.md) — `ssl.ca.location`, `client.id`, `debug`, etc. — plus `schema.registry.url` to decode JSON-schema topics. Names are checked when the query is bound (a misspelling is a Binder Error); topic-level properties such as `auto.offset.reset` are not accepted. Values pass to librdkafka unchanged.

description:
Read messages from a Kafka topic as DuckDB rows. Multi-partition topics are scanned in parallel by partition. Each row is `(topic, partition, offset, key, message)`; the key and message are `BLOB`s you decode in SQL based on your serialization (JSON, Avro, Protobuf, etc.), or `JSON` columns when `schema.registry.url` points at the topic's JSON schemas.

Each scan reads every non-empty partition from its first retained offset up to the high watermark seen when the scan started, without joining a consumer group or committing offsets. `WHERE` filters run after the read, so scope cost by snapshotting into a table, and use `tributary_metadata` first to plan the scan.

examples.description: Snapshot a topic into a local table
examples.code:
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE orders_snapshot AS
SELECT *
FROM tributary_scan_topic('orders',
                          "bootstrap.servers" := 'kafka:9092');

examples.description: Decode JSON messages on the way in
examples.code:
SELECT
  partition,
  "offset",
  json_extract_string(decode(message), '$.user_id') AS user_id,
  json_extract_string(decode(message), '$.event')   AS event
FROM tributary_scan_topic('events',
                          "bootstrap.servers" := 'kafka:9092');

examples.description: SASL-authenticated consume through a cluster secret

name: tributary_metadata

returnsTable.name: brokers
returnsTable.description: Array of broker descriptors — id, host, port.

returnsTable.name: topics
returnsTable.description: Array of topic descriptors — name, error, partitions[]. Each partition includes its leader, replicas, and ISR set.

parameters.name: bootstrap.servers
parameters.description: Comma-separated `host:port` list of brokers to bootstrap from.
Any other librdkafka global (client) property — same surface as [`tributary_scan_topic`](#tributary_scan_topic). This function doesn't read `tributary_cluster` secrets.

description: Inspect a Kafka cluster without consuming from a specific topic. Returns one row containing two arrays: `brokers` and `topics`. Useful for discovering what a cluster exposes, sizing partition-parallel scans, or scripting topic-list audits.

examples.description: List every topic on a cluster
examples.code:
SELECT unnest(topics).name AS topic_name
FROM tributary_metadata("bootstrap.servers" := 'kafka:9092');

SELECT
  t.name                            AS topic,
  array_length(t.partitions)         AS partitions
FROM (
  SELECT unnest(topics) AS t
  FROM tributary_metadata("bootstrap.servers" := 'kafka:9092')
)
ORDER BY partitions DESC;
